summary: Brighton Beach Front Range Light, on the North (Yorke) River at Charlottetown Harbour, was built in 1889 to lead ships through a narrow channel; a 1900 gale felled its rear tower, and the city took the front light over in 2013.

structures.note: Coast Guard list gives tower height 12.5 m; Lighthouse Friends gives 12.2 m (40 ft); the 11.0 m in the record is the focal height on the Coast Guard list. Register dates the front light to 1889; Lighthouse Friends gives 1889 as start of work, 1890 as first lit, and 1892 for skeleton towers.
Skeleton towers by James Hanrahan, $383.90; mast lights of 1890 replaced; the upper parts were enclosed with wooden lanterns (Lighthouse Friends).
Completed 24 December 1968 (Lighthouse Friends). Coast Guard lists the rear light at 26.3 m focal height, 18.4 m tower, hexagonal tower.

access.note: Lighthouse Friends: grounds and tower closed. It stands on a crib in the river.

facts.agency: City of Charlottetown (owner since 2013); light listed by the Canadian Coast Guard

events.note: Construction of the first Brighton Beach range lights begins; the register dates the front light to 1889
Range lights put into operation on the opening of general navigation (Lighthouse Friends); the record gives 1892
Mast lights replaced by skeleton towers with wooden lanterns, built by James Hanrahan for $383.90
Red diamond daymarks painted on the channel faces of the front and rear towers
Rear range tower blown down in a heavy gale on 11 October 1900; a temporary light was shown from a lantern hoisted between two poles
Foundation started for the front range light (report for the year ended 30 June 1906); Lighthouse Friends dates the new cribwork to 1907
A 25 mm diamond vapour installation replaces the duplex lamp at the front light (report for the year ended 31 March 1909)
Front range light moved to a new site
Front range light moved again; new concrete foundation built
Wooden tower of the rear range light destroyed by fire, around 1930
Lights electrified; last keeper John Francis Duffy retires; A. A. LeClair appointed caretaker at $50 a year
Rear range light's concrete apple-core tower completed on 24 December 1968
Front range light severely damaged by a storm surge in winter 2000; top 6 m cut off and bottom rebuilt
Coast Guard proposal for slab, shorter tower, vinyl siding and new deck is rejected by Charlottetown city council
Council accepts the only bid, $146,700 from Ostridge Brothers, to restore the front light; work carried out that summer
Front range transferred from federal ownership to the City of Charlottetown, ceremony 12 September 2013

keepers.name: John Francis Duffy

corrections.proposed: 12.5 (tower height on the Coast Guard list); 11.0 m is the focal height
corrections.why: The record's 11.0 m matches the Coast Guard's focal height for the front light, not the tower height. The Coast Guard's list gives the tower as 12.5 m, and Lighthouse Friends gives 12.2 m. The record's 11.0 m also appears under light.focal_height_m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives first lit 1892. Lighthouse Friends says the range lights went into operation in 1890 and the skeleton towers came in 1892. The register dates the front light to 1889, the year work began. Story uses the register's date for construction and Lighthouse Friends for the first light.

notes_for_editor: (1) Lighthouse Friends is the main source for the keepers and the post-1952 history (the 2009 proposal, the 2012 contract, the 2013 transfer). The Department's keepers' table in the 1904 volume (fiscal year ended June 30, 1903, printed p. 220, scan 233) gives James Lewis at the Brighton Beech Range on 1 March 1899; the position of that entry was matched by OCR column, and the 1903 volume (scan 246) prints the same name, station and date on one line. Galvin, Hughes, Dalziel and Duffy are not confirmed by name in the corpus. A 1912-1915 Department table places J. Purcell at the Brighton beach range (matched by position in the OCR); this is not used in the story. The printed page 69 read for the 1903 volume's row was inferred from the OCR headers and not checked on the image. (2) The front light's date: the register says 1889 for the front light; Lighthouse Friends says work began in 1889, lights came into use in 1890, and skeleton towers were built in 1892. The register's description (a square tapered wooden tower) is of the present tower, but the sources do not say which year that tower was built. The story says so. (3) The record's first_lit 1892 against Lighthouse Friends' 1890 (range lights in use). (4) The record's 11.0 m is the Coast Guard focal height; the tower is 12.5 m on the same list (12.2 m per Lighthouse Friends). (5) Wikipedia's Brighton Beach Range Lights article gives 1890 as the build date; it is a lead only and was not cited. (6) The 1906 report's crib sentence is cut off in the OCR; the words 'foundation was started' are matched, and 'crib' is not in the quote. Check scan page 47 before quoting it further. (7) The 1909 vapour-lamp item is matched to the front light by the report's own heading ('Brighton Beach, Front Light'). (8) The Department's 1900 storm entry says 'back range light tower'; the rear light is the one blown down, as Lighthouse Friends says. (9) The 2000 storm surge and the 2009-2013 events have no source other than Lighthouse Friends; a news search could corroborate them but was not run. (10) Access: Lighthouse Friends says "Grounds/tower closed" (corrected in the 2026-10-27 check; the first draft said no source gave access). (11) No photos sourced.
